title: Number Sense
description: Understand counting, place value, and the structure of whole numbers.

lessons.title: Counting and Place Value
objectives: Read and write multi-digit whole numbers

pedagogy.title: Place value columns
pedagogy.content: From right to left: ones, tens, hundreds, thousands, ten-thousands.

pedagogy.title: Remember the order
pedagogy.content: Ones, Tens, Hundreds: O-T-H sounds like 'oath'—make a promise to always start from the right.

content.content: Every digit in a number has a value based on its position. In 4,573, the digit 5 is in the hundreds place, so it represents 500.
In 28,406, the digit 8 is in the thousands place and represents 8,000.

exercises.question: In the number 6,249, what value does the digit 4 represent?
hints: Start from the right: ones, tens, hundreds, thousands.
The 4 is two places from the right.
exercises.solution: The digit 4 is in the hundreds place, so it represents 400.

exercises.question: What is $3000 + 200 + 50 + 7$?
hints: Add the thousands, hundreds, tens, and ones separately.

exercises.question: Draw a place-value chart for 5,318 and label each digit.
hints: Use columns for thousands, hundreds, tens, and ones.
exercises.solution: A chart with 5 in thousands, 3 in hundreds, 1 in tens, and 8 in ones.

lessons.title: Comparing and Ordering Numbers
objectives: Order numbers from least to greatest

pedagogy.title: Line up digits
pedagogy.content: When comparing two numbers, align them by place value and compare from the leftmost digit.

content.content: Use the symbols > (greater than), < (less than), and = (equal to) to compare numbers. The open side of the symbol always faces the larger number.

exercises.question: Which statement is true?
hints: Compare the hundreds first, then tens, then ones.
exercises.solution: Both numbers have 4 hundreds. 481 has 8 tens while 472 has 7 tens, so 472 < 481.

lessons.title: Rounding Whole Numbers
objectives: Round whole numbers to a given place value

pedagogy.title: 5 or more, raise the score
pedagogy.content: Look at the digit to the right of the target place. If it is 5 or greater, round up. Otherwise, round down.

content.content: Rounding makes numbers easier to work with by replacing them with nearby multiples of 10, 100, or 1000.
Round 738 to the nearest hundred. The tens digit is 3, which is less than 5, so 738 rounds to 700.

exercises.question: Round 856 to the nearest hundred.
hints: The tens digit is 5, so round up.
exercises.solution: The tens digit is 5, so 856 rounds up to 900.

lessons.title: Introduction to Fractions
objectives: Understand fractions as parts of a whole

pedagogy.title: Numerator and denominator
pedagogy.content: The denominator tells how many equal parts the whole is divided into. The numerator tells how many parts you have.

content.content: A fraction represents a part of a whole. If a pizza is cut into 8 equal slices and you eat 3, you ate 3/8 of the pizza.

exercises.question: A rectangle is divided into 6 equal parts. Shade 2/6 of the rectangle.
hints: Divide the rectangle into 6 equal parts if needed.
exercises.solution: Two out of six equal parts should be shaded.

exercises.question: In the fraction $\frac{5}{9}$, what does the 9 represent?
hints: The bottom number is the denominator.
options: The number of parts you have
The total number of equal parts
exercises.solution: The denominator 9 means the whole is divided into 9 equal parts.
